question: Using elementary row transformations, examine whether the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&2\\2&3&5\\3&4&7\end{bmatrix}$$ can be transformed into the identity matrix, and hence determine whether $A^{-1}$ exists.

options.A: $A$ can be transformed into $I_3$, so $A^{-1}$ exists
options.B: Row reduction produces a zero row, so $A$ cannot be transformed into $I_3$ and $A^{-1}$ does not exist
options.C: Row reduction produces $I_3$ after one additional row interchange, so $A^{-1}$ exists
options.D: The matrix is already equivalent to $I_3$ without producing any zero row, so $A^{-1}$ exists
